headline: Learned and reduced models map protein conformational transitions and binding dynamics
label: Protein Conformational Dynamics Modeling
summary: Coarse-grained neural potentials and diffusion-bridge models now sample unbound-to-bound and ternary complex transitions without MSAs.
synthesis: The dominant thread is computational sampling of biomolecular conformational space through reduced or learned representations. AMARO v2.0 employs a coarse-grained neural network potential that retains heavy atoms with implicit solvent to sample protein-ligand and ternary complex dynamics. K-Fold models unbound-to-bound transitions with a diffusion bridge, without MSAs. DA2-GRASP pairs a variational autoencoder with guided generative sampling to map folding pathways at lower computational cost than MD, and the FGFR3 study combines Gaussian-accelerated MD, beta-VAE, and Markov state models to resolve an activation landscape with allosteric pathways. Other items address association mechanisms via multiscale kinetic Monte Carlo, hydrogen-bond network analysis, quantum-walk residue prioritization, and maximum-entropy reweighting for HDX-MS, so the set is methodologically heterogeneous. The shared element is the attempt to link learned or reduced models to interpretable transition pathways, though the items do not share a single method.
